profile.reading:
Csquare ORD4 sits at 4513 Western Avenue, Lisle, Illinois 60532, in what Csquare's own materials describe as the Illinois Technology and Research Corridor. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's own spec page states 66,875 square feet of raised floor at ORD4, but its SEC Form S-1 property table gives a substantially larger figure, 110,066 square feet for "ORD4_A," 74.7 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026, a roughly 43,000 square foot gap this profile flags rather than resolves, since it is far larger than the minor rounding differences seen across Csquare's other Chicago-area sites and could reflect a different measurement basis or an unreconciled building-phase difference. Csquare's spec page states 88.9 megawatts of utility power for ORD4, a figure notably disproportionate to its stated square footage compared with ORD1 and ORD2, alongside 3.6 megawatts of UPS capacity and 14 megawatts of generator capacity; this profile reports these figures as published by Csquare rather than adjusting them, while flagging the apparent inconsistency. Compliance certifications include SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001; unlike ORD2, Csquare does not cite a formal Uptime Institute Tier rating for ORD4. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for ORD4.

Lisle sits within DuPage County's technology corridor along the East-West Tollway (Interstate 88), historically home to Bell Labs, AT&T, and Lucent Technologies research and operations facilities that helped establish the area's telecommunications infrastructure legacy well before Csquare's current ownership. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, making ORD4 one of three Csquare-branded Chicago-area sites alongside ORD1 in downtown Chicago and ORD2 in Elk Grove Village.

reading.body:
Centersquare's Lisle ORD4 campus publishes 147.6 MW of combined utility power across 237,000 square feet of technical space. The published figure is combined utility power, not a stated IT load, so the usable IT capacity is lower by an amount that is not published. If IT load runs at a common colocation ratio of roughly 75 percent of utility draw, that implies approximately 110 MW of IT power, which, at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, is roughly 2,750 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common mixed-workload density, it is roughly 11,000 racks. Those are illustrative estimates, not the operator's claims.

The five certifications the operator publishes qualify this campus to host specific categories of regulated workload. SOC 1 Type 2 covers financial reporting controls, making it eligible for finance-sector tenants with audit requirements. SOC 2 Type 2 covers security, availability, and related trust criteria, qualifying it for cloud and enterprise tenants with data-handling obligations. PCI DSS qualifies it for environments that process payment card data. ISO 27001 is an internationally recognized information security management standard. NIST 800-53 aligns the facility with the control framework used by US federal agencies and their contractors.

Among the 44 facilities this site has mapped in Illinois, only 6 publish a megawatt figure, together totaling 236 MW. ORD4's 147.6 MW places it seventh by published capacity in the state, which means six Illinois facilities have individually published larger figures. That ranking reflects only what operators have chosen to disclose to this site, not the full installed base of the state.
